Time-Domain Simulation

Complete API for time-domain simulation.

Quick Start

using Powerful, PowerFlowData, DifferentialEquations

# 1. Load power flow case
case = PowerFlowData.parse_network("cases/ieee14.raw")
sys_pf = SystemModel(case)

# 2. Solve power flow
prob_pf = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys_pf)
sol_pf = solve(prob_pf, NewtonRaphson())

# 3. Load dynamic models (example with DYR file)
# dynamic_data = PowerFlowData.parse_dyr("cases/ieee14.dyr")
# dynamic_models = create_dynamic_models(dynamic_data)

# 4. Create and solve TDS problem
prob = TDSProblem(sys_pf, sol_pf, dynamic_models; tspan=(0.0, 5.0))
sol = solve(prob)  # Uses Rodas5P() by default

# 5. Extract results
data = collect_state_trajectory(sol, prob)  # Returns NamedTuple
# df = DataFrame(data)  # Convert to DataFrame if needed

TDS Infrastructure

Core TDS problem types, workspaces, and residual evaluation from solvers/tds.jl.

Powerful.TDSConfig — Type
TDSConfig

Runtime configuration for Time-Domain Simulation.

These settings control solver behavior and can be loaded from TOML configuration files.

Fields

  • convert_pq_to_zip::Bool: Convert PQ loads to ZIP model during TDS setup (default: false)
  • p_zip::NTuple{3,Float64}: Active power ZIP composition (Z%, I%, P%), must sum to 1.0 (default: (0.0, 0.0, 1.0) = constant power)
  • q_zip::NTuple{3,Float64}: Reactive power ZIP composition (Z%, I%, P%), must sum to 1.0 (default: (0.0, 0.0, 1.0) = constant power)
  • flat_start::Bool: Use flat start for initialization (default: false)
  • abstol::Float64: Absolute tolerance for DAE solver (default: 1e-6)
  • reltol::Float64: Relative tolerance for DAE solver (default: 1e-3)
  • maxiter::Int: Maximum iterations for implicit solver (default: 10)

ZIP Model

The ZIP model represents load as combination of:

  • Z (constant impedance): P ∝ V², Q ∝ V²
  • I (constant current): P ∝ V, Q ∝ V
  • P (constant power): P = const, Q = const

Example TOML

[solver.TDS]
convert_pq_to_zip = true
p_zip = [0.3, 0.3, 0.4]  # 30% Z, 30% I, 40% P for active power
q_zip = [0.2, 0.3, 0.5]  # 20% Z, 30% I, 50% P for reactive power
abstol = 1e-8

Example Julia

settings = TDSConfig(
    convert_pq_to_zip = true,
    p_zip = (0.3, 0.3, 0.4),
    q_zip = (0.2, 0.3, 0.5)
)
source
Powerful.TDSInitialization — Type
TDSInitialization

Initial conditions computed from power flow solution.

This is Phase 2 of TDS construction - the "where we start". Contains state values at t=0 for all dynamic models.

Fields

  • dyn::NamedTuple - Per-model states: (GENROU=(delta=[], omega=[]), ...)
  • setpoints::NamedTuple - Setpoint values: (GENROU=(P_m0=[], E_q0=[]), ...)
  • pf::NamedTuple - Power flow snapshot: (v=[], theta=[])

Construction

init = TDSInitialization(tds_sys)

Inspection

init.dyn.GENROU.delta      # Initial rotor angles
init.dyn.GENROU.omega      # Initial speeds (should be ~1.0)
init.setpoints.TGOV1.P_m0  # Mechanical power setpoints
source

Compute initial conditions from power flow solution.

Uses the linking information in tds_sys to gather data from power flow and compute initial states for all dynamic models.

source
Powerful.TDSProblem — Type
TDSProblem

Time-domain simulation problem specification.

Fields

  • sys::SystemModel - System with dynamic models (from add_dynamic_models)
  • formulation::FormulationTrait - DAE formulation (PowerInjection or CurrentInjection)
  • tspan::Tuple{Float64, Float64} - Time span (tstart, tend)
  • events::Vector - Events (faults, load changes, etc.) - placeholder for Phase 9
  • init::NamedTuple - Initialization data with subfields:
    • dyn: Per-model initialized states (GENCLS=(delta, omega, ...), ...)
    • setpoints: Per-model setpoints for holding equations (GENCLS=(Pm0, Eq0), ...)
    • pf: Power flow snapshot (v=[], theta=[])

Construction

sys_tds = add_dynamic_models(sys_pf, sol_pf, dynamic_models)
prob = TDSProblem(sys_tds; tspan=(0.0, 10.0))

Note

This struct follows the DifferentialEquations.jl problem pattern. Users will call solve(prob, IDA()) with SciML solvers.

source
Powerful.TDSProblem — Method
TDSProblem(sys_pf, sol_pf, dyn_models; tspan, config, kwargs...)

Convenience constructor for TDS problems (wraps staged construction).

For most users, this single-call API is sufficient. Use the staged API (TDSSystem + TDSInitialization) when you need to inspect intermediate results.

Arguments

  • sys_pf::SystemModel - Power flow system model
  • sol_pf::PowerFlowSolution - Converged power flow solution
  • dyn_models::NamedTuple - Dynamic models (e.g., from parse_dyr)

Keyword Arguments

  • tspan::Tuple - Simulation time span (default: (0.0, 1.0))
  • config::SimConfig - Simulation configuration (default: SimConfig())
  • Other kwargs passed to TDSProblem(tds_sys, init; ...)

Example

# Simple one-liner
prob = TDSProblem(sys_pf, sol_pf, dyr_data; tspan=(0.0, 10.0))
sol = solve(prob)

# Equivalent staged construction (for debugging)
tds_sys = TDSSystem(sys_pf, sol_pf, dyr_data)
init = TDSInitialization(tds_sys)
prob = TDSProblem(tds_sys, init; tspan=(0.0, 10.0))
source

Powerful.TDSProblem — Method
TDSProblem(tds_sys::TDSSystem, init::TDSInitialization; kwargs...)

Create a TDS problem from staged construction types.

This is the recommended constructor for TDS problems, providing full inspectability of intermediate results.

Arguments

  • tds_sys::TDSSystem - System with dynamic models (from Phase 1)
  • init::TDSInitialization - Initial conditions (from Phase 2)

Keyword Arguments

  • tspan::Tuple - Simulation time span (default: (0.0, 1.0))
  • formulation::FormulationTrait - DAE formulation (default: PowerInjection())
  • events::Vector - Disturbance events (default: empty)

Example

# Staged construction with inspection
tds_sys = TDSSystem(sys_pf, sol_pf, dynamic_models)
init = TDSInitialization(tds_sys)

# Debug: check initial conditions
@show init.dyn.GENCLS.omega  # Should be ~1.0

prob = TDSProblem(tds_sys, init; tspan=(0.0, 10.0))
sol = solve(prob)

Powerful.TDSSystem — Type
TDSSystem

System with dynamic models merged and linked to static models.

This is Phase 1 of TDS construction - the "what" of the simulation. Contains system topology and model linking, but no state values yet.

Fields

  • sys::SystemModel - Merged system (static + dynamic models)
  • links::ModelLinks - Dynamic → static model mapping
  • pf_sol::PowerFlowSolution - Power flow solution (for initialization)

Construction

tds_sys = TDSSystem(sys_pf, sol_pf, (GENROU=genrou, TGOV1=tgov1))

Inspection

tds_sys.links.source_type   # [:GENROU, :GENROU, :TGOV1, ...]
tds_sys.links.target_idx    # Which static instance each replaces
keys(tds_sys.sys.models)    # All model types in merged system
source

CommonSolve.solve — Method
solve(prob::TDSProblem; alg=nothing, use_mass_matrix::Bool=true, kwargs...)

Solve time-domain simulation problem using data stored in prob.

Uses the unified architecture with ADCache and thin adapters.

Arguments

  • prob::TDSProblem - TDS problem with initialization data
  • alg - Solver algorithm (optional)
  • use_mass_matrix - Use mass matrix formulation (default: true)
  • kwargs... - Passed to DifferentialEquations.solve()

Example

# Basic usage
prob = TDSProblem(sys_pf, sol_pf, dynamic_models)
sol = solve(prob; abstol=1e-8, reltol=1e-6)

# With disturbance events
prob = TDSProblem(sys_pf, sol_pf, dynamic_models;
    tspan=(0.0, 10.0),
    events=[BranchTrip(1.0, 1, 5, "1")]
)
sol = solve(prob)
source
Powerful.apply_zip_conversion! — Method
apply_zip_conversion!(sol::PowerFlowSolution, settings::TDSConfig)

Convert PQ loads to ZIP model while preserving power consumption at operating voltage.

This implements PSS/E's "Reconstruct loads using present voltage" operation. The converted load will consume the same power at the solved voltage as before.

ZIP Model

After conversion, load power consumption becomes voltage-dependent:

  • P = pl + ipV + ypV² (constant power + current + impedance)
  • Q = ql + iqV + yqV²

Algorithm

For each load at operating voltage V_op:

# Compute total consumption at operating point
P_total = pl + ip*V_op + yp*V_op²
Q_total = ql + iq*V_op + yq*V_op²

# Redistribute to maintain same consumption at V_op
yp_new = z% × P_total / V_op²   # Constant impedance (Z)
ip_new = i% × P_total / V_op    # Constant current (I)
pl_new = p% × P_total           # Constant power (P)

Arguments

  • sol::PowerFlowSolution: Solved power flow (provides PQ models and bus voltages)
  • settings::TDSConfig: Settings containing p_zip and q_zip tuples

Notes

  • Modifies sol.prob.sys.models.PQ in place
  • Power consumption is preserved at the operating voltage
  • Uses foreign variable mechanism to get voltage at each load's bus

Example

sol = solve(ACPowerFlowProblem(sys), NewtonRaphson())
settings = TDSConfig(
    convert_pq_to_zip = true,
    p_zip = (0.3, 0.3, 0.4),  # 30% Z, 30% I, 40% P
    q_zip = (0.2, 0.3, 0.5)   # 20% Z, 30% I, 50% P
)
apply_zip_conversion!(sol, settings)

See Also

  • TDSConfig: Configuration struct with ZIP percentages
  • validate: Validates that ZIP percentages sum to 1.0
source
Powerful.collect_state_trajectory — Method
collect_state_trajectory(sol, prob::TDSProblem; include_time=true) -> NamedTuple

Extract all differential state variables from TDS solution as a NamedTuple.

Returns a NamedTuple with columns for time (optional) and all state variables, with automatic naming: model_variable_instance (e.g., GENCLS_delta_1).

The returned NamedTuple can be directly converted to a DataFrame if DataFrames.jl is loaded: df = DataFrame(collect_state_trajectory(sol, prob)).

Arguments

  • sol: DifferentialEquations.jl solution object
  • prob::TDSProblem: TDS problem (for variable metadata)
  • include_time::Bool: Include time column (default: true)

Returns

NamedTuple with fields:

  • t: Time vector (if include_time=true)
  • model_variable_instance: One field per state variable (e.g., GENCLS_delta_1)

Example

prob = TDSProblem(sys_pf, pf_sol, dyn_models; tspan=(0.0, 10.0))
sol = solve(prob)

# Get as NamedTuple
data = collect_state_trajectory(sol, prob)
println(data.GENCLS_omega_1)  # Access specific variable

# Convert to DataFrame (if DataFrames.jl is loaded)
using DataFrames
df = DataFrame(data)

# Save to CSV
using CSV
CSV.write("tds_results.csv", df)
source
Powerful.create_model_links — Method
create_model_links(sys_pf::SystemModel, dynamic_models::NamedTuple) -> ModelLinks

Build links between dynamic models and power flow models using trait methods.

Returns struct-of-arrays for efficient vectorized operations.

Algorithm

  1. For each dynamic model type, call get_replacement_map()
  2. For each target type in map, match instances by field values
  3. Convert external IDs to internal indices during matching
  4. Return ModelLinks struct-of-arrays

Example

links = create_model_links(sys_pf, (GENCLS=gencls_models,))
# Returns links mapping each GENCLS instance to its PV/Slack counterpart
source
Powerful.get_state_variable_info — Method
get_state_variable_info(prob::TDSProblem) -> Vector{NamedTuple}

Get metadata for all differential state variables in the TDS problem.

Returns a vector of variable information in address order, where each entry contains:

  • model::Symbol - Model name (e.g., :GENCLS)
  • variable::Symbol - Variable name (e.g., :delta, :omega)
  • instance::Int - Instance index (1-based)
  • address::UInt - Address in state vector

Example

prob = TDSProblem(sys_pf, pf_sol, dyn_models; tspan=(0.0, 10.0))
state_info = get_state_variable_info(prob)

for info in state_info
    println("$(info.model).$(info.variable)[$(info.instance)] @ address $(info.address)")
end
# Output:
#   GENCLS.delta[1] @ address 1
#   GENCLS.delta[2] @ address 2
#   GENCLS.omega[1] @ address 3
#   ...
source
Powerful.validate — Method
validate(settings::TDSConfig)

Validate TDS settings. Throws ArgumentError if invalid.

Checks:

  • p_zip components sum to 1.0 (±1e-6 tolerance)
  • q_zip components sum to 1.0 (±1e-6 tolerance)
  • All ZIP components are non-negative

Powerful.InitContext — Type
InitContext

Bundles all data needed for dynamic model initialization into a single context.

This eliminates parameter sprawl in initialize_dynamic_states and provides a clean interface for models to access:

  • Power flow solution and system
  • Model links (pre-filtered per model via helpers)
  • Previously initialized model states (accumulated during initialization loop)

Fields

  • pf_sol::PowerFlowSolution: Completed power flow solution
  • sys::SystemModel: TDS system with dynamic models
  • links::ModelLinks: All model links
  • initialized::Dict{Symbol, NamedTuple}: Accumulated initialized states

Usage

# Driver creates context once
ctx = InitContext(pf_sol, sys, links)

# Each model uses helper to get its data
data = gather_init_data(ctx, GENCLS)  # Returns NamedTuple from init_sources
source
Powerful.InitInputKind — Type
InitInputKind

Abstract type for initialization input resolution strategies.

Concrete subtypes determine how to resolve an InitInput declaration:

  • FromObservation: Computed PF quantities (P, Q via compute_observations)
  • FromSolution: Direct PF state variables (V, θ)
  • FromPriorState: Previously initialized model states (e.g., P_m from GENCLS)
source
Powerful.InitializationOrder — Type
InitializationOrder

Topologically sorted initialization sequence.

Fields

  • models_by_group::Dict{Symbol, Vector{Symbol}} - Model types per group
source
Powerful.compute_initialization_order — Method
compute_initialization_order(sys::SystemModel) -> InitializationOrder

Compute initialization order from model metadata using topological sort.

Dependencies are inferred automatically from InitInput declarations:

  • InitInput(:prior_state, ...) → depends on the group of from_model
  • InitInput(:observation, ...) or InitInput(:solution, ...) → depends on :power_flow

Algorithm

  1. Collect all models and their declared groups
  2. Build model → group lookup for dependency resolution
  3. Infer dependencies from InitInput metadata
  4. Topological sort to determine group order
  5. Validate no cycles exist (Kahn's algorithm detects cycles)

Throws

  • ErrorException if circular dependencies detected
source

Powerful.gather_init_data — Method
gather_init_data(ctx::InitContext, ::Type{M}) -> NamedTuple

Resolve all initialization inputs for a model type using its metadata declarations.

This is the main helper for model initialization - it eliminates boilerplate by:

  1. Extracting targetmodels and targetindices from ctx.links
  2. Getting model metadata
  3. Calling resolveinitinputs with the context

Arguments

  • ctx::InitContext: Initialization context with pf_sol, links, and accumulated states
  • ::Type{M}: Model type (e.g., GENCLS, TGOV1)

Returns

NamedTuple with fields matching the model's init_inputs declarations.

Example

function initialize_dynamic_states(model::StructArray{GENCLS{T}}, ctx::InitContext) where T
    data = gather_init_data(ctx, GENCLS)
    # data.P_gen, data.Q_gen, data.V_bus, data.theta_bus available
    # ... model-specific computation
end
source
Powerful.get_initialization_group — Method
get_initialization_group(::Type{<:AbstractModel}) -> Symbol

Declare which initialization group this model belongs to.

Dependencies between groups are automatically inferred from InitInput(:prior_state, ...) declarations - no explicit dependency declaration needed.

Groups are initialized in dependency order. Common groups:

  • :power_flow - Power flow models (Bus, PQ, PV, Slack, Branch)
  • :generators - Synchronous machine dynamics (GENCLS, GENROU, etc.)
  • :exciters - Excitation systems (EXST1, SEXS, etc.)
  • :turbine_governors - Prime movers (TGOV1, HYGOV, etc.)
  • :stabilizers - Power system stabilizers (STAB1, etc.)
  • :loads - Dynamic loads

Default: :uncategorized (initialized last)

Example

get_initialization_group(::Type{<:GENCLS}) = :generators
get_initialization_group(::Type{<:EXST1}) = :exciters
source
Powerful.initialize_dynamic_states — Method
initialize_dynamic_states(model::StructArray{<:AbstractModel}, ctx::InitContext) -> NamedTuple

Initialize ALL instances of a dynamic model at once using the initialization context.

This is a trait function that dynamic models implement. The default implementation errors, requiring models to provide their specific initialization logic.

Arguments

  • model::StructArray - All instances of the dynamic model (for type dispatch)
  • ctx::InitContext - Context with pf_sol, sys, links, and accumulated initialized states

Returns

NamedTuple of state arrays (one vector per state variable)

Example Implementation

function initialize_dynamic_states(model::StructArray{GENCLS{T}}, ctx::InitContext) where T
    # Use helper to gather all declared init_sources
    data = gather_init_data(ctx, GENCLS)

    # Model-specific computation using data.P_gen, data.Q_gen, etc.
    # ...

    return (delta=delta, omega=omega, ...)
end
source
Powerful.resolve_init_inputs — Method
resolve_init_inputs(
    ctx::InitContext,
    target_models::Vector{Symbol},
    target_indices::Vector{Int},
    metadata::ModelMetadata
) -> NamedTuple

Resolve all initialization inputs declared in model metadata using type-dispatched resolution.

Algorithm

For each InitInput declaration in metadata:

  1. Get the input kind via get_input_kind(Val(input.kind))
  2. Dispatch to appropriate resolve_input method
  3. Collect results into NamedTuple

Arguments

  • ctx::InitContext: Initialization context with pf_sol, sys, links, and accumulated states
  • target_models::Vector{Symbol}: Linked model types for each instance (e.g., [:PV, :PV, :Slack])
  • target_indices::Vector{Int}: Indices into linked model arrays
  • metadata::ModelMetadata: Model metadata with init_inputs declarations

Returns

NamedTuple with one field per InitInput entry, each containing a vector of values.

Example

# GENCLS initialization
target_models = [:PV, :PV, :Slack]
target_indices = [5, 8, 3]

metadata = model_metadata(GENCLS)
data = resolve_init_inputs(ctx, target_models, target_indices, metadata)

# Returns: (P_gen=[2.0, 1.5, 3.5], Q_gen=[0.5, 0.3, 1.2], V_bus=[1.05, 1.03, 1.04], ...)
data.P_gen[1]  # 2.0 - Active power for GENCLS[1] from PV[5]
source

resolve_input(::FromObservation, ctx, input, target_models, target_indices) -> Vector{Float64}

Resolve input from power flow observations (computed quantities like P, Q).

Handles heterogeneous linked models (e.g., some GENCLS link to PV, others to Slack), each with their own compute_observations implementation.

source
Powerful.resolve_input — Method
resolve_input(::FromPriorState, ctx, input, target_models, target_indices) -> Vector{Float64}

Resolve input from previously initialized model states.

Used by models that depend on other models' initialized states (e.g., TGOV1 needs GENCLS's P_m). The initialization order ensures dependent models are initialized after their dependencies.

Example

# TGOV1 instances link to GENCLS instances
# ctx.initialized contains: Dict(:GENCLS => (P_m = [1.0, 1.5, 2.0], ...))
# input.field = :P_m

tm0 = resolve_input(FromPriorState(), ctx, input, [:GENCLS, :GENCLS], [1, 2])
# → [1.0, 1.5]
source

Validation & Diagnostics

Tools for validating TDS initialization and diagnosing issues from solvers/tds_validation.jl.

ResidualValidationResult

Residual validation check results.

Fields

  • max_diff_residual::Float64 - Maximum absolute differential residual
  • max_alg_residual::Float64 - Maximum absolute algebraic residual
  • non_zero_diff::Vector{Tuple{UInt, Float64, Symbol, Symbol}} - (address, value, model, equation)
  • non_zero_alg::Vector{Tuple{UInt, Float64, Symbol, Symbol}} - (address, value, model, equation)

Powerful.validate_tds_initialization — Method
validate_tds_initialization(prob::TDSProblem; atol=1e-6, max_show=20)

Validate TDS initialization by checking that residuals are zero at t=0.

Uses get_initial_conditions to evaluate residuals at initial time and checks if they satisfy steady-state conditions (f=0, g=0).

Arguments

  • prob::TDSProblem - Initialized TDS problem
  • atol::Float64 - Absolute tolerance for zero check (default: 1e-6)
  • max_show::Int - Maximum violations to include in result (default: 20)

Returns

ResidualValidationResult with diagnostics

Example

prob = TDSProblem(sys_pf, sol_pf, dynamic_models)
result = validate_tds_initialization(prob)

if !result.is_valid
    println("Max residual: ", result.max_alg_residual)
end
source
